Subject: Confidentiality breach carve-out — request for forensics notice and remedies

Hi Monica / Rishi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we move toward finalizing the MSA + Order Form, our security and legal teams flagged the proposed liability cap language. For clarity: Acme needs a narrowly tailored carve-out from the cap for breaches that trigger trade-secret exposure or authorized-access exfiltration.

Two asks from our side:
- A short forensics/notice protocol so we can investigate measures and remediate quickly (timeline, contact points, evidence preservation).
- Limited monetary remedy carve-out if trade secrets are demonstrably exfiltrated (we expect this to be narrowly scoped and linked to confirmed forensic findings).

Can your legal team propose specific language and an operational flow? I'm attaching a simple diagram of our internal incident intake and what we would expect from a vendor (for context).

Thanks,
Samantha Young

Subject: Re: Confidentiality breach carve-out — request for forensics notice and remedies

Samantha,

Appreciate the clear summary. We can accommodate a narrowly scoped carve-out linked to confirmed forensic evidence, but need to make it operational so it doesn't swallow the cap. High-level proposal:

- Trigger: confirmed trade-secret exfiltration as evidenced by mutually agreed forensic firm report (see attached draft flow).
- Notice: vendor (Acme) provides initial written notice within 48 hours of suspected exfiltration and preserves logs/KV caches for 7 days unless agreed otherwise.
- Scope: monetary damages tied to actual documented loss (no punitive/treble damages); carve-out capped at a multiple of the most recent 12-month fees or a fixed floor (we propose $500k floor or 3x ARR, whichever is lower).
- Evidence: mutually agreed shortlist of minimum evidence items (hashes, audit logs, sample exfiltrated artifact).
- Remediation: expedited patching and rollback assistance with timeline commitments.

I asked Legal (Marissa) to prepare redline language for the MSA/Order Form. If that looks workable we can include the forensic flow as an annex and a DocuSign route for expedited acknowledgement.

Attaching: forensics-notice-flow.pdf; I also uploaded a draft redline to the Drive link below.

Best,

Folks — drafting notes and redline summary below. Quoted for context: 

> "Trigger: confirmed trade-secret exfiltration as evidenced by mutually agreed forensic firm report"

Key points in our proposed redline (high level):
1) Trigger and standard of proof
- We will accept a forensic report from an independent firm agreed within five business days. The report must identify the data items at issue and show a plausible chain of custody.

2) Preservation and access
- Redwood will preserve relevant system logs, KV cache snapshots, and network captures for 14 days on notice and provide secure access to Acme's authorized forensics team. Requests for longer preservation require a court order or mutual written agreement.

3) Monetary carve-out mechanics
- Carve-out limited to direct losses attributable to the confirmed exfiltration. No consequential, incidental, or punitive damages.
- Carve-out ceiling: $500,000 OR 2x the 12-month committed spend under the Order Form, whichever is lower. (Rationale: protects customer while keeping exposure bounded for Redwood.)

4) Mitigation and offsets
- Redwood's mitigation efforts (timely patching, notification, root cause analysis) reduce liability dollar-for-dollar for costs Redwood reasonably incurred.

5) Confidentiality re: forensics reports
- Forensics report is confidential and subject to the MSA NDA; sharing beyond defined recipients requires redaction or consent.

Open items for negotiation:
- Floor vs. multiplier choice (customer prefers a larger remedy floor; we prefer multiplier tied to fees).
- Timeline for independent firm selection and whether Acme can appoint interim firm pending agreement.

I'll attach the redline and track changes in the Drive folder. Rishi — can you loop in Sales Execs if this materially changes commercial terms? Vivek — please confirm if the 14-day preservation is acceptable from an operational standpoint or whether we should shorten to 7 days.

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal, Contracts
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Marissa / Monica — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear redline. Acme can agree in principle to the mechanics you propose with one change request: we need the preservation window to be 14 days (minimum) as drafted, and we want the carve-out cap to be the greater of $500k or 1.5x the 12-month committed spend (Acme argues a floor protects customers of varying sizes).

Two practical asks before we proceed to signature: 
- DocuSign flow for the forensics annex so both parties have an operational acceptance (we don't want the annex to be inadvertent back-and-forth post-signature).
- A short, mutually agreed list of required evidence items (we will accept hashes + samples + audit logs; Redwood to provide a template evidence checklist).

If you can accept the small cap tweak (floor OR multiplier with floor prevailing when larger), we can run final approval on Monday and return a countersigned MSA + Order Form.

Dana Lawson
Counsel, Acme Robotics
dlaw@acmelegal.com
